sentences.text:
The present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred seeking following reliefs:-
(i) An order or direction may kindly be issued awarding the compensation amount to the petitioner under the law land acquisition act.
(ii) That an accountability may kindly be fixed against the authority in respect of petitioner grievance.
(iii) If the compensation is not granted to the petitioner, direction may kindly be issued against the respondent authority to restore the land area as agriculture land.
(iv) Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the case may also be granted in the interest of justice.

2. It is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the owner of land bearing survey No.93 admeasuring 2.276 hectares situated at village Mehmoodganj Tehsil Lateri District Vidisha and is in possession thereof.

It is further submitted that since a road was constructed without acquiring the land belonging to the petitioner, he moved a writ petition No.952/2011, which Malkhan Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143486905/

sentences.text: w i t h N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2026:MPHC-GWL:11269 2 WP-11350-2026 following directions:-

"Having heard the counsel for the parties, this Court is of the view that an inquiry is inevitable as regards the complaint of the petitioner of acquisition of land of his ownership for construction / broadening of road in view of para 2 of the impugned communication by the Tahsildar to the Collector.

Accordingly, this Writ Petition is disposed of with directions that the petitioner shall submit a detailed representation with relevant documents in support of his claim of acquisition of land without compensation within fifteen days.
In turn, the respondents shall constitute a committee of revenue officers for the purpose of enquiry into the matter with due opportunity to the petitioner.

In the event it is found that the land of the petitioner's ownership has been acquired for construction / broadening of the road in question,
the petitioner shall be given the benefit of compensation in accordance with law.
Let this exercise be completed within three months from the date of submission of certified copy of the order passed today."
3. In pursuance to the directions issued by this Court, representations were moved by the petitioner before the Revenue Authorities but because of boundary dispute, the matter could not be decided.

The petitioner thus moved an application on 14.01.2019 and 28.01.2020 but on an objection raised by the other side, proceedings under Section 145 of MPLRC were initiated vide case No.3/145/2020,
which were dismissed vide order dated 16.09.2021.

The petitioner thereafter again moved an application before the Tehsildar for demarcation of his land, however, since the demarcation was not done, another writ petition No.19445/2022 was preferred, which was disposed of vide order dated 29.08.2022 with liberty to the petitioner to file fresh application for demarcation of the land before the competent authority

. In pursuance to the aforesaid directives, a fresh application was moved by the petitioner for demarcation which according to the petitioner have been decided vide order dated 26.06.2025, but even then the claim for compensation by the competent authority has not been decided so far.
4. Learned counsel further submits that since the dispute with regard to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11269 3 WP-11350-2026 demarcation has already come to an end vide order dated 26.06.2025 and there is no legal impediment for the competent authority to decide the claim for compensation

, the competent authority may be directed to decide the application/claim for compensation regarding the land acquisition for construction of the road in a time bound manner and if such directions are issued, grievance of the petitioner would be redressed.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State submits that if such directions are issued, the claim of the petitioner for compensation shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

6. After hearing rival contentions and perusing the record, this Court without going into the merits of the matter, deems it expedient to direct the competent authority (Land Acquisition) to decide the claim of the petitioner for compensation within a period of three months from the date of receiving the certified copy of this order.
